data.title: Holiday headache: A strike threat looms at the ports of L.A. and Long Beach
data.description:
The retail sector faces a potential headwind in front of the holiday season as a potential strike of security guards at the Port of Los Angeles and Port of Long Beach looms.

The Pacific Maritime Association noted it failed to reach a labor deal with a local union that represents 250 security guards at the two major ports ahead of the current contract’s expiration at 12:01 a.m. on Saturday. The guards already voted last month to authorize a strike. The unarmed guards work at six important container-handling terminals that are responsible for moving more than half of the Los Angeles-Long Beach ports’ containers. While the security guards represent a small percentage of the workforce at the ports, employers warned other unionized dockworkers would refuse to cross picket lines.

The two sides are expected to meet again at the bargaining table on Friday.

A strike at the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach has the potential to disrupt supply chains for major U.S. importers and retailers across consumer goods, furniture, electronics, and apparel, just in front of the holiday season. The list of major retailers that could be impacted includes Walmart (WMT), Target (TGT), Amazon (AMZN), Home Depot (HD), Lowe's (LOW), Best Buy (BBY), Nike (NKE), Five Below (FIVE), and Dollar Tree (DLTR). Retail ETFs potentially in harm's way include the SPDR S&P Retail ETF (XRT), VanEck Retail ETF (RTH), Amplify Online Retail ETF (IBUY), ProShares Online Retail ETF (ONLN), and Direxion Daily Retail Bull 3X Shares (RETL).

data.title: Activist Carronade raises Brookdale stake above 5%, wants changes - Reuters
data.description:
Activist Carronade Capital has raised its stake in Brookdale Senior Living (BKD)  above 5% and wants ‌the largest operator of senior housing in the US to increase its share price.

Carronade is looking for changes in how the company allocates its capital and how it looks at its M&A strategy, according to a Reuters report on Thursday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

Carronade owned a ~4% stake in Brookdale (BKD) as of Sept. 30.

The activist ⁠has been in contact with management and is expected to step up its engagement to discuss possible portfolio optimization, better disclosure to investors, and a potential transformation into a real estate investment ​trust, according to the report. 
 
A Brookdale representative didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
 
Brookdale (BKD) is scheduled to present at the  Stephens Annual Investment Conference | NASH2026 at 12:45 EST today.

data.title: NXP Semiconductors started with Buy rating at StoneX on auto chip growth
data.description:
StoneX initiated coverage of NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) with a Buy rating and a $340 price target, saying the chipmaker offers exposure to a broader semiconductor recovery without relying heavily on the AI data center boom.

"We see NXPI as one of the cleanest ways to play the broadening chip cycle without taking risk from the growing concerns surrounding the AI data center trade and the capital intensity surrounding it," said analysts highlighting that its data center exposure accounts for less than 5% of its expected fiscal 2026 revenue.

StoneX sees growth coming from automotive chips, particularly new processors for software-defined vehicles, improving manufacturing margins and shareholder returns.

The brokerage expects NXP's S32N and S32K5 processor platforms to drive growth as automakers increasingly adopt software-defined vehicle architectures. Management is targeting about $2B in software-defined vehicle revenue in 2027.

StoneX also expects gross margins to improve as new 300-millimeter manufacturing facilities come online, potentially reaching 60% in 2027.

A new $5B share buyback authorization, bringing total available repurchases to $6.3B, also supports its investment case, StoneX said.

data.title: Suspected Houthi strike damages Saudi wealth fund’s Riyadh tower
data.description:
A suspected Houthi missile damaged Riyadh’s tallest skyscraper on Thursday, shattering windows and damaging the exterior of the Public Investment Fund’s headquarters, Reuters reported. Authorities evacuated people and restricted access to the surrounding King Abdullah Financial District. No casualties were immediately reported.

For investors, the attack highlights security risks facing Saudi Arabia’s effort to attract foreign capital and expand beyond oil. Repeated strikes on its financial hub could undermine business confidence, disrupt operations and complicate investment plans central to the kingdom’s economic transformation.

Three sources told Reuters that a Houthi missile struck the tower. The Saudi-led coalition said it had responded to a missile threat and reported falling debris and property damage. The Houthis offered no immediate comment. An attack on November 8 also damaged Aramco’s (ARMCO) building in the district.

The escalation comes as Saudi officials anticipate potentially six more months of fighting, Reuters reported. Since hostilities resumed in July, Houthi territorial advances in Yemen have weakened Saudi-backed forces. Continued fighting, alongside broader regional tensions, threatens to prolong uncertainty for businesses and investors.

data.title: Merlin appoints Bob Smith as interim CEO
data.description:
Merlin (MRLN) announced Wednesday that its board of directors has appointed Bob Smith, a member of the Board, as chairman and interim chief executive officer, effective November 18, 2026.

The company highlighted that Smith succeeds founder Matt George, who has resigned as chief executive officer, Chairman, and a member of the board of directors and has transitioned to the role of founder and advisor. 

The firm added that Smith brings more than three decades of aerospace and defense leadership. As chief executive officer of Blue Origin from 2017 to 2024, he transitioned the company from a research organization into an operating business, growing annual sales from nearly zero to more than $750M and building an order book of approximately $10B.

Previously, he spent more than a decade at Honeywell Aerospace, including as president of Mechanical Systems and Components, a business with more than $4 billion in annual revenue, and as chief technology officer, responsible for more than 12,000 engineers and technologists.

Before Honeywell, he worked on upgrading the NASA space shuttle at United Space Alliance. He also currently serves as a senior advisor to the Office of the Secretary of Defense as part of the Business Operators for National Defense (BOND) program and as a director of Parsons Corporation.

Source: press release

data.title: Merck inks cancer research deal with AI drug discovery firm Isomorphic Labs
data.description:
Merck (MRK) is joining hands with AI-driven drug discovery firm Isomorphic Labs to discover drug candidates against cancer, the companies announced on Thursday.

As part of the collaboration, Isomorphic Labs will leverage its drug design engine (IsoDDE) and data sets supplied by Merck (MRK) to discover small molecules against an undisclosed oncology target.

The pharma giant will be responsible for their preclinical and clinical studies, as well as manufacturing and commercialization of the treatments resulting from the deal.

Per the terms, Isomorphic Labs will be eligible for an upfront payment and subsequent payments tied to R&D, regulatory, and commercial milestones.

The London-headquartered firm will also receive tiered royalties based on net sales of commercialized products and an option that allows it to earn higher royalties if it joins Merck (MRK) to fund their development activities.

data.title: GlobalFoundries in spotlight as Wedbush sees humanoid trialing as positive step
data.description:
• GlobalFoundries (GFS) was in the spotlight on Thursday as Wedbush Securities said the company trialing Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid is a positive step for the semiconductor foundry.
  • “While near-term financial impact is likely immaterial, we see the partnership as consistent with GF’s push toward automation and predictive maintenance to improve utilization and cost competitiveness, particularly at its higher-cost US and European sites,” Wedbush Securities analyst Matt Bryson wrote in a note to clients. “Longer term, robotics adoption is also a potential demand driver for the power, sensing, and connectivity chips that sit squarely in GF’s specialty portfolio.”
  • Media reports have indicated that Boston Dynamics will begin field testing Atlas at a key GlobalFoundries site early next year. That would make GlobalFoundries the first customer for Atlas outside the automotive industry. 
  • GlobalFoundries is also expanding its use of Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped robot, which has been used at its Vermont fab for more than four years, to its New York, Dresden, and Singapore locations.

data.title: Marsh's Oliver Wyman to acquire Synpulse, terms undisclosed
data.description:
Marsh's (MRSH) management consulting business, Oliver Wyman, is set to acquire technology consulting and AI platform company Synpulse.

Synpulse serves banks, insurers, wealth managers, and other financial services organizations. 

Terms of the deal were not disclosed.

The transaction is expected to close in early 2027.
